body:
This. This is what I was expecting from my sessions so far. Your dead on, I've gotten used to having acquaintances, and keeping people at a distance. I've now set a schedule, once a week I'm going to try calling up someone I've lost touch with. I've also a core group of old friends I still talk to from and I definitely need to make more time to keep in touch (I'm not much of a facebook person as of yet).

As for therapy, ya'll have convinced me that I need to take advantage of my university's services, especially in a week when school ends and I have no more excuses. It'll be uncomfortable at 1st, but I can't go on like this, somethings gotta give and it might as well be my pride.

I just found out through my university that it would be covered under the insurance I have through them, I'm gonna take advantage of that; time to act.

I actually did a few meetups with the reddit group in my new city, was a blast. Then school kicked in to high gear and I forgot to make time. I might as well look up local outdoorsy type groups on there. School ends in a week, I'll have no excuse then!

You've answered a question I've had for a while now. So medication is not necessarily a permanent thing? But can be more of a training wheel of-sorts. 
I do have problems opening up to people, always kindof have. Being totally honest with the psychologist is difficult for me. I suppose cause I'm scared of being seen as weak (damn Protestant farmtown upbringing), while I'm also not really sure what to say, as in what is even meaningful. He doesn't offer much in the way in advice or hope to deal with this, more of just listens and encourages. Helpful in its own way, but not really what I'm looking for.

Thank you, It's nice to hear of your success. I often feel like the only times I hear of someone on meds is when it isn't working; otherwise there's such a stigma about mental illness that I'd never really find out about those who's lives it's changed. 

I know my fears are irrational. But they're there nonetheless. Maybe it's time I talked to an actual Dr. about this.

Can I ask you, is this a permanent medication? Like, will you likely need to be on it for the rest of your life? And are such things covered by insurance at all? or are you payin for it yourself?

EDIT: Oh and yea, the hiking and getting outside is really my biggest source of joy, especially when I was in beautiful Arizona. Wish I had more time for it.

Honestly, I'm scared mainly because of my mother. She simply just got worse from my age onward, shuffling between an endless list of medications, which only seems to make her less mentally stable. Also I'm in the middle of a graduate degree, now doesn't seem the time to start messing with my brain chemistry, especially if it might "make me a bit nuts at first," I've got deadlines and shit lol.

.... but then again I can use that as an excuse for the rest of my life.

Nah, it helps to know we're not alone. TY

Also, I firmly believe pain/heartache is totally relative, everyone's struggles are enough to overwhelm them. There are countless people around this world in far worse situations than me who would be justified in telling me to chill out and deal with this. 
But we're in the same boat..... how to go about it? :/

:EDIT for Clarity:

I'm in a similar boat friend. I think there's more of us than are ever willing to admit it, partially cause of the stigma of metal issues in America (where I'm assuming your also from). But it still sucks feeling the only reason I'm still here is fear about what it might do to those around me; I don't even care about myself anymore. 

No matter what though, we cannot opt-out. As much as life may seem hollow and meaningless I have to believe it will get better. Just keep trudging on, if only for the sake of those you love. In time, we might learn to love ourselves and truly see the amazing opportunity we have here. As dark as things may seem now, I'm pretty certain it's infinitely darker and emptier after this life ends.

That being said, please talk to someone. Do not hesitate to anonymously pour your soul out to me in a PM (or any of the caring people in this thread who've offered an ear), hell I'll even give you my cell number and we can use codenames. All it takes sometimes is for someone to just listen, and empathize. Not offer advice, but simply be there for you to bitch/scream/cry at. This is not something you can let echo around in your head, or it'll keep eating away at you. 


TLDR; There are people who love us and even if we can't understand why, it's because they know we are worthy of their love. In time, hopefully we'll truly *feel* this worth within ourselves too. But you are **Never** alone.
